raw_response:
I've been working these fields since I was a young woman. I know this land. Let me think through what I'll do.

My two hands and my husband's — that's all the labor we have. At 68, I can't push myself too hard, so I keep things manageable. Cotton is my cash crop — I always put most of my land in cotton. It's hard work to pick, but I know cotton. I'll put 7 mu in it. For the cotton seeds, I buy hybrid seeds from the village supply store like everyone else does now. I'll plant after the last frost in late April.

Maize I grow for our own food and to sell the extra. 4 mu is enough — we don't need more than that for two people. I always buy hybrid maize seeds, everyone around here does, the yields are better.

My Chinese cabbage goes in after summer — that's the autumn planting. I'll use 3 mu. I save my own cabbage seeds from good plants each year, like my mother taught me. Same with chili — I have my own seeds I've been keeping for years. Chili takes a lot of bending over to harvest, so I keep it small, just 1.5 mu.

For fertilizer, I do what I've always done — put base fertilizer down before planting, then top-dress when the plants need it. Cotton gets the most because it's my income. I use compound fertilizer plus urea. Cabbage needs good feeding too if I want big heads.

Irrigation from my well — I'll water when the soil looks dry and before the critical growth stages. Cotton I'll water at budding, flowering, and boll setting. Maize at jointing and silking. Cabbage when it's heading up.

Pesticides — cotton still gets aphids and bollworms so I spray regularly. Cabbage gets caterpillars. I spray when I see the pests, not on a fixed schedule, but cotton always needs more attention.

I use rotary tillage — I rent the machine from the village. It's easier on my back than ploughing by hand.
